TESTDESIGN.label: decision of this test plan
TESTDESIGN.loc: a threshold chosen here because no source publishes one. Stated as a decision, never as a measurement. The first built unit's measured value replaces it.

equipment: Assembly stand / test jig
holds the robot with both feet clear of the bench
`robotctl robot init` MOVES EVERY JOINT and ramps to the home pose over ~2 s. The cheatsheet is explicit: 'have the robot on its stand'. Every test before WK runs on the stand
CHEAT
Bench PSU, 0-15 V, >= 5 A, adjustable current limit
stands in for the pack for every test up to EB-05
a 2S Li-ion pack into an unproven board is a fire. The pack is not fitted until EB-01..EB-05 have passed
TESTDESIGN
DMM, 4.5 digit, DC V to 0.001 V, DC A to 10 A
every rail in section 3
the rail bands are stated to 3 dp; a 3.5-digit meter cannot resolve the 3.130-3.470 V gate
TESTDESIGN
DC current clamp or shunt, >= 25 A
servo-rail current during the walk test
15 x stall at 5.0 V = 22.05 A is a number the vendor rows support. Nothing in any source says what the pack or the HAT path can deliver, so the instrument must not be the limit
XLPART
Dynamixel TTL adapter (U2D2 or equivalent) + 3-pin JST EH lead
SV-01 single-servo ID assignment, off the robot
EEPROM writes need one servo alone on the bus, because every unassigned servo answers to ID 1
E1
Oscilloscope >= 100 MHz with one 10x probe
optional: bus signal integrity at 1,000,000 bps on a 16-device multidrop line
only needed when SV-03 finds intermittent devices
TESTDESIGN
White 88 % reflectance target, >= 200 x 200 mm, matte
SN-05 ToF ranging
88 % white is the reflectance ST's own maximum-range and accuracy tables are stated against; any other target invalidates the +/- 5 % gate
L8
Steel rule or laser distance meter, 1 mm resolution
SN-05 target distance; WK-02 walked distance
the +/- 5 % ToF gate at 500 mm is +/- 25 mm, so the reference distance must be better than that
TESTDESIGN
Digital inclinometer, 0.1 deg
levelling the walk surface
the walk gate is a distance in 8 s; a sloped bench moves it
TESTDESIGN
Laptop with a microphone and an FFT tool, or a USB measurement mic
SN-07 audio
the fitted speaker and microphone parts are both CANNOT DETERMINE, so the audio gate is functional (a tone comes out and goes back in), not acoustic
EVER
Bluetooth gamepad, Xbox-style
WK-02..WK-04 and SW-05
`padd` drives whatever pad connects; pairing is once per pad
CHEAT
Flat hard level bench, >= 1200 x 600 mm
WK-02 walk run
see the surface note in section 7
TESTDESIGN

rails.where: NP-F550 pack terminals, and again at the banana contact PCB output
rails.nominal: 7.2 V (Duracell DR5) / 7.4 V (Deity, Viltrox) — the two 2S nominal conventions
rails.basis: 8.40 V = 2 x 4.20 V fully charged off charger; 6.60 V = the runtime's own empty floor, BATTERY_EMPTY_V, which is also 0 % on the gauge and where robotd sits the robot down

rails.net: SERVO_V (XL330 VDD, pin 2 of the 3-pin JST EH)
rails.where: pin 2 of the first bus cable at the HAT end (cable 1, dxl-hat-id34), and again at the farthest ankle (id24, id14)
rails.nominal: UNRESOLVED — this measurement is the point of test EB-04
rails.band: vendor operating band 3.70 – 6.00 V (recommended 5.00 V); the runtime instead maps 6.60 – 8.20 V read through this very pin
rails.basis: E1 Specifications 'Input Voltage | 3.7 ~ 6.0 [V] (Recommended : 5.0 [V])' against model.rs:99-113. The two cannot both be true of a stock servo. NOT a defect of this plan — the open question the plan exists to close

rails.net: HAT 5V (to the Radxa, 40-pin header pins 2 and 4)
rails.where: header pin 2 or 4 to header pin 6 (GND)
rails.basis: Radxa states only 'DC +5V' and '5V/2A' with NO tolerance in any fetched document — the +/- 5 % band is a decision of this plan, not a vendor figure. Record the measured value to 3 dp whatever the verdict

rails.where: the codec's AVDD pin, and the Stemma J5 3V3 pin
rails.basis: the tightest fitted-part band on this rail: VL53L8CX AVDD 3.13 / 3.30 / 3.47 V (Table 12). Wider parts on the same rail: BMI088 VDD 2.4-3.6 V, TLV320AIC3104 AVDD/DRVDD 2.7-3.6 V, LSM6DSV16X Vdd 1.71-3.6 V. If the fitted ToF is a VL53L5CX instead, that part runs a single 3V3 for AVDD+IOVDD and the band relaxes; the L8CX band is the safe one to hold either way

TLV320AIC3104 digital core DVDD 1.525-1.95 V (nominal 1.8). KNOWN OPEN on our reconstruction: in electronics/robot-hat/ this rail dead-ends on test point TP1 (decision D5) and no 1.8 V source is designed in — a board built from our files will read 0 V here and that is a defect of the board, not of the unit

rails.where: VL53L8CX CORE_1V8 pin on the ToF breakout
rails.basis: VL53L8CX Table 12 CORE_1V8 1.62/1.80/1.98 V. The VL53L5CX has NO separate core rail — if the fitted sensor is the L5CX this pin does not exist and the row is N/A, not FAIL

rails.nominal: 1.20 V or 1.80 V, per the module's strapping
rails.basis: VL53L8CX Table 12. Which configuration the fitted breakout uses is CANNOT DETERMINE — read the module's own schematic before judging this rail

rails.where: FPC pin 15 at the camera board
rails.basis: the Seeed IMX219 module datasheet gives a 3.3 V module supply on FPC pin 15 but no tolerance; the bare sensor's internal rails are 2.8 V analog / 1.8 V interface / 1.2 V digital and are generated on the camera board. Record the measured value; no gate is asserted

rails.where: the Radxa's USB 2.0 OTG Type-C port
rails.basis: the overlay disables the FUSB302/ET7301B PD controller at /i2c@fe5c0000/fusb302@22; its power-on defaults present Rd on both CC lines so any charger still supplies 5 V. Whether the pack charges in situ is CANNOT DETERMINE and EB-08 is the measurement

registers.name: Baud Rate
registers.why: robotd opens the port at 1 Mbps. A servo left at the factory 57,600 cannot be reached at all, so this is one of the two values that MUST be set at build time

registers.name: ID
registers.why: fifteen servos share one multidrop bus. The ID cannot be self-assigned on a shared bus, so it is set one servo at a time. Range 0~252; 254 (0xFE) is the broadcast ID and is never assigned

registers.name: Protocol Type
registers.why: already the factory value; read it back rather than writing it, so a servo that has been used elsewhere is caught

registers.name: Return Delay Time
registers.why: robotd writes this at every boot (model.rs:82-94). 250 x 16 devices = 8 ms per tick, 40 % of a 20 ms tick, so a bus that has not had it cleared cannot hold 50 Hz. Writing it at build time makes the first boot honest

registers.name: PWM Slope
registers.why: robotd asserts it at boot. Note an internal disagreement on the vendor page: the table row says range 1~255, the description says 0~255. Recorded, not resolved

registers.name: Shutdown
registers.means: Bit 5 Overload, Bit 4 Electrical Shock, Bit 2 Overheating latch; Bit 0 Input Voltage Error CLEARED
registers.why: robotd clears exactly the input-voltage fault. That is consistent with the servos seeing the raw 2S pack above their 6.0 V rating. It is an observation on Pollen's code, NOT a vendor recommendation, and EB-04 is what turns it into a fact

registers.name: Temperature Limit
registers.why: the gate for WK-05. Not written by robotd; verified so a servo returned from another project cannot come in with a lowered limit

registers.name: Max Voltage Limit
registers.means: the firmware refuses to be told to accept more than 7.0 V
registers.why: the ceiling is BELOW the pack's 8.2 V full. Read it back on every servo; it is the register that makes the SERVO_V question unavoidable

registers.name: Current Limit
registers.means: the maximum the firmware will command
registers.why: the gate for EB-07. This is a LIMIT, not a measured draw: no running current is published for this servo at any voltage, only standby 17 mA and stall 1.11/1.47/1.74 A at 3.7/5.0/6.0 V

registers.name: Torque Enable
registers.why: E1: 'Data in the EEPROM Area can only be written when the value of Torque Enable(64) is cleared to 0'. Every EEPROM step below is gated on this

registers.name: Position P Gain
registers.why: RAM, so a power cycle restores the vendor initial 400. robotd rewrites it. Standing uses x0.8 = 160; limp-fall uses 50

registers.name: Position I Gain
registers.why: vendor initial is already 0; robotd writes it anyway

registers.name: Position D Gain
registers.why: CORRECTION to docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md 3.3, which says a power cycle 'restores factory D'. The vendor initial value of Position D Gain(80) is 0, so a power cycle restores D = 0, not a non-zero damping term

registers.name: Present Position
registers.why: the measurement behind SV-05 and SV-06

registers.name: Present Current
registers.means: 1 mA, measured AT THE INPUT POWER SOURCE (not phase current) on the XL330 series
registers.why: the measurement behind EB-07, and it needs no meter

registers.name: Present Input Voltage
registers.why: the only voltage the robot can read about itself: there is no fuel gauge and no ADC. EB-06 checks it against a meter, and its 0.1 V quantisation IS the tolerance of that check

sections.title: Electrical bring-up

tests.title: Pre-power continuity and short check
tests.purpose: Find a short before a 2S pack finds it.
pre: Robot assembled to the point where the banana contact PCB, the HAT and the Radxa are fitted and the servo bus is UNPLUGGED.
No battery fitted. No bench supply connected.

steps.do: Measure resistance BAT+ to GND at the banana contact PCB output.
Measure resistance HAT 5V (header pin 2) to GND (header pin 6).
Measure resistance HAT_3V3 to GND at the Stemma J5 connector.
Measure resistance SERVO_V (pin 2) to GND (pin 1) at the HAT's bus header.

tests.measure: Four resistances, ohms.

gate.PASS: every measured resistance > 100 ohm
gate.FAIL: any measured resistance < 10 ohm
gate.CD: between 10 and 100 ohm — a low but non-zero reading is an inrush-capacitor charge path on some rails and a fault on others; identify which by the schematic before powering

tests.gate_basis: The 10 ohm / 100 ohm split is a decision of this plan. No source states an expected cold resistance for any of these nets, because the Robot HAT and the banana PCB are unpublished.

tests.title: First power-on, bench supply, no pack, no servos
tests.purpose: Bring the board up behind a current limit that cannot start a fire.
pre: EB-01 PASS.
Servo bus unplugged at the HAT. Camera and ToF unplugged.
Bench supply set to 7.40 V, current limit 0.50 A, output OFF.

steps.do: Connect the supply in place of the pack, at the banana contact PCB output. Observe polarity: BAT+ / BAT-.
Enable the output and watch the supply's current readout for 5 s.
steps.expect: the supply does not enter constant-current

steps.do: Record the settled current.

tests.measure: Settled input current at 7.40 V, in A to 3 dp.

gate.PASS: the supply stays in constant-voltage for 5 s and the settled current is recorded
gate.FAIL: the supply enters constant-current at 0.50 A — power down immediately and return to EB-01

tests.gate_basis: No quiescent-current figure exists for the assembled Microduck in any source. This test RECORDS the number for the first time; the 0.50 A limit is a decision of this plan, chosen to be above a Radxa Zero 3W booting (Radxa specifies a 5 V/2 A adapter, i.e. up to 10 W, but states no idle draw) and far below anything that damages a board.

tests.title: Rail survey
tests.purpose: Every supply the fitted parts need, measured at the pin that needs it.
pre: EB-02 PASS, supply still at 7.40 V.
Sensors reconnected one at a time, re-checking the current after each.

steps.do: Work down the rail table in section 3.1, probing at the stated point with the stated reference.

tests.measure: One DC voltage per rail, to 3 dp, plus the reference point used.

gate.PASS: every rail with a band is inside it
gate.FAIL: any rail with a band is outside it
gate.CD: a rail whose band is CANNOT DETERMINE (camera 3V3, ToF IOVDD) — record the value and say so; it is not a pass

tests.gate_basis: Bands come from the fitted parts' own datasheets, tightest-part-wins per rail; see section 3.1 for the basis of each row. The 5 V band is the one decision of this plan on this table.

tests.title: SERVO_V — the measurement that settles the open question
tests.purpose: Determine whether the XL330 servos are fed the raw 2S pack (6.6-8.4 V, above their 6.0 V rating) or a regulated rail.
pre: EB-03 PASS.
Servo bus plugged in, all 16 devices connected, torque OFF (no robotd running).
Bench supply raised to 8.20 V, current limit 3.00 A.

steps.do: Measure pin 2 (VDD) to pin 1 (GND) at the HAT end of cable 1 (dxl-hat-id34).
Measure pin 2 to pin 1 at the far end of the chain, at id24 and at id14.
Compute the drop from the HAT to each ankle.
Repeat all three with the supply at 6.60 V (the empty-pack case).

tests.measure: Four DC voltages per supply setting, to 3 dp, and the two computed drops.

gate.PASS: the measurement is taken at all four points at both supply settings and recorded. Either result is a valid outcome of THIS test.
gate.FAIL: the measurement is not taken, or the harness drop from the HAT to the farthest ankle exceeds 0.550 V at 8.20 V in

tests.gate_basis: 0.550 V is the total HAT-to-farthest-ankle drop our own harness model computes for AWG 21 at 8.2 V with 1 A per moving servo (wiring/CABLES.md, cecad.harness.check_drop, PASS at every hop). It is a model, and this test is what checks it. On the outcome: if SERVO_V tracks the supply, production Microducks run stock XL330s 0.6-2.2 V above the vendor's 6.0 V maximum, which is consistent with robotd clearing the Input Voltage Error bit of Shutdown(63); if SERVO_V sits inside 3.7-6.0 V, the HAT regulates and docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md 3.4 must be corrected.

tests.title: Bus standby current
tests.purpose: Confirm every device on the bus is actually powered before anyone asks it to move.
pre: EB-04 PASS. Supply at 7.40 V, torque off everywhere.
tool: Bench PSU readout or DMM in series

steps.do: Record the total input current with all 16 devices connected and idle.
Subtract the EB-02 board-only figure to get the servo-rail standby.

tests.measure: Total input current and the derived servo-rail standby, in A to 3 dp.

gate.PASS: the derived servo standby is >= 0.255 A AND SV-03 finds all 16 devices
gate.FAIL: SV-03 finds fewer than 16 devices
gate.CD: the current is below 0.255 A but SV-03 finds 16 devices — the current path and the data path disagree; do not proceed

tests.gate_basis: 0.255 A = 15 x 17 mA, the vendor's Standby Current for the XL330-M288-T (E1 Specifications; no test voltage is stated for it). The imu_to_dxl board's own standby is CANNOT DETERMINE (unpublished board), so this is a floor and not a window. The devices answering on the bus is the stronger evidence, which is why SV-03 is in the gate.

tests.title: Pack fitted: what the robot reads against what a meter reads
tests.purpose: Cross-check the only voltage the robot can measure about itself.
pre: EB-05 PASS. Bench supply removed. A charged NP-F550 pack fitted.
robotd running, torque off.

steps.do: Measure the pack terminals with a meter.
Read every servo's Present Input Voltage(144), 0.1 V per count.
steps.expect: a voltage on the health row

steps.do: Compare. Note that robotd reads the pack THROUGH the servos: there is no fuel gauge and no ADC anywhere on this robot.

tests.measure: Meter voltage to 3 dp; the register value in counts and in volts.

gate.PASS: |V_meter - V_register| <= 0.100 V
gate.FAIL: the difference exceeds 0.100 V
gate.CD: the register reads nothing — 'batt not read yet' on the monitor means no tick has completed; fix that first

tests.gate_basis: 0.100 V is the register's own quantisation: Present Input Voltage(144) is 0.1 V per count (E1 Control Table). It is the tightest honest tolerance for this comparison and it is a vendor figure, not a choice.

tests.title: Running current in three states
tests.purpose: Close the gap the vendor leaves: no running current is published for this servo at any voltage.
pre: SV-05 PASS (home pose verified). Pack fitted and charged. Robot on the stand.

steps.do: State A - torque off, bus idle. Record pack current for 10 s.
State B - `robotctl robot init`, home pose held, no command, 30 s.
State C - walking at vx 0.25 m/s for 8.0 s (see WK-02). Record simultaneously.
In every state, log Present Current(126) for all 15 servos from the state stream.

tests.measure: Pack current mean and peak per state (A, 3 dp); per-servo Present Current(126) mean and peak (mA).

gate.PASS: no servo's Present Current(126) reaches Current Limit(38) = 1750 mA in any state
gate.FAIL: any servo reaches 1750 mA, or any servo latches on Overload (Shutdown bit 5)
gate.CD: the clamp cannot be fitted — then the per-servo register readings stand alone and the pack figure stays unmeasured

tests.gate_basis: 1750 mA is Current Limit(38)'s initial value and its maximum, verbatim from E1's EEPROM table — the most the firmware will command, not a measured peak. The vendor stall rows are 1.11 / 1.47 / 1.74 A at 3.7 / 5.0 / 6.0 V; above 6.0 V no vendor figure exists, which matters directly if EB-04 finds SERVO_V on the raw pack. Present Current on the XL330 series is measured at the input power source, not phase current (E1 Current Limit(38) note).

tests.title: USB-C behaviour with the pack fitted
tests.purpose: Answer, on a unit, what no document answers: which port powers, and whether the robot charges in place.
pre: EB-06 PASS.
tool: USB-C 5 V supply with a current readout

steps.do: With the pack fitted and the robot off, connect 5 V to the USB 2.0 OTG Type-C port. Record VBUS, the current drawn, and whether the pack voltage rises over 10 min.
Repeat on the USB 3.0 HOST Type-C port.
Repeat both with the pack removed.

tests.measure: VBUS (V, 3 dp), current (A, 3 dp), pack voltage before and after 10 min (V, 3 dp), per port and per pack state.

gate.PASS: the four cases are measured and recorded
gate.FAIL: the board draws current on a port and does not come up
gate.CD: this is the expected verdict on the charging question until a unit is measured

tests.gate_basis: The overlay disables the PD controller at /i2c@fe5c0000/fusb302@22 (fitted silicon is an ET7301B on the public Radxa schematics, an FUSB302B-compatible clone that binds the same driver at 0x22); its power-on defaults present Rd on both CC lines so any charger still gives 5 V. Which port charges, and whether in-situ charging happens at all, is listed CANNOT DETERMINE in docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md 9 and 12.12. Note the MCP73213 reference charger on the shelf needs roughly 8.7 V or more at its input, which 5 V USB cannot provide - so an in-robot 2S charge from USB-C would require a boost stage nobody has seen.

sections.lede: Nothing here assumes a pack. The order is deliberate: find a short with a meter, bring the board up behind a current limit, survey the rails at the pin that needs them, and only then plug in 2S Li-ion. Test EB-04 is the reason this section exists in this form - it is the measurement that settles whether production Microducks run their servos above the vendor's rating.

sections.title: Servo identity and calibration

tests.title: ID and baud assignment, one servo at a time
tests.purpose: Give each servo the identity the bus needs. This is the only per-unit EEPROM value that cannot be self-assigned.
pre: Servo out of the robot, or fitted but with its lead the only one on the adapter.
Dynamixel TTL adapter connected, servo powered at 5.00 V from the bench supply (the vendor's recommended operating point).

steps.do: Scan at 57,600 bps (Baud Rate(8) initial value 1). Expect exactly one device at ID 1.
Write Torque Enable(64) = 0.
Write ID(7) = the assigned ID from the map in section 4.1.
Write Baud Rate(8) = 3.
Power-cycle the servo, re-scan at 1,000,000 bps.
steps.expect: one device at the assigned ID

steps.do: Write, then read back: Return Delay Time(9) = 0, PWM Slope(62) = 255, Shutdown(63) = 52.
Read back and record, do not write: Protocol Type(13) = 2, Temperature Limit(31) = 70, Max Voltage Limit(32) = 70, Min Voltage Limit(34) = 35, Current Limit(38) = 1750.
Write a label with the ID on the servo case before it goes back in the robot.

tests.measure: Per servo: the eleven register values read back after the power cycle.

gate.PASS: every written register reads back exactly the written value, and every verify-only register is at its factory value
gate.FAIL: any read-back differs, or the servo does not answer at 1 Mbps after the power cycle
gate.CD: a verify-only register differs from factory — the servo has been used elsewhere; restore it and re-run rather than accepting it

tests.gate_basis: Every value and every initial value here is quoted verbatim from E1's control table in ce-parts/xl330-m288-t/electrical.chip.json. EEPROM writes are gated on Torque Enable(64) = 0 by the vendor's own rule.

tests.title: Horn indexing and mechanical zero
tests.purpose: Set the joint's zero by assembly, because there is no homing register in play.
pre: SV-01 PASS for this servo.
The bracket or link that bolts to this horn is in hand.

steps.do: Torque Enable(64) = 1 and command Goal Position = 2048 (0 rad).
Fit the link so the joint sits at the MJCF zero pose for that joint, then bolt through the horn's 4 x M2 tapping screws on PCD 12.
Torque Enable(64) = 0 and read Present Position(132).

tests.measure: Present Position(132) in counts at the fitted zero.

gate.PASS: |Present Position - 2048| <= 11 counts (= 0.967 deg)
gate.FAIL: |Present Position - 2048| > 11 counts

tests.gate_basis: 2048 = 0 rad on a 4096 pulse/rev 12-bit encoder (E1 Specifications; bus.rs). 11 counts is 1.0 deg at 0.0879 deg/count, and 1.0 deg is the amplitude of the backlash twins the policies were trained against (const.py, docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md 10.3) - the tightest published mechanical uncertainty on this joint. NOTE: the XL330's horn is a 4-hole pattern on PCD 12, so a mis-index is 90 deg = 1024 counts and cannot hide inside this gate. IMPORTANT: robotd never writes Homing Offset. Zero is mechanical, set here, and there is no register that can rescue a badly fitted horn.

tests.title: Bus roll-call at 1 Mbps
tests.purpose: Sixteen devices, one wire. Prove all sixteen are there before anything is asked to move.
pre: Robot fully wired per wiring/CABLES.md. Power on. robotd STOPPED (two writers on one UART corrupt each other's replies).
tool: robotd's own init path, or a Dynamixel scan tool

steps.do: Stop the daemon and scan the bus.
Broadcast-ping at 1,000,000 bps, Protocol 2.0, on /dev/ttyS2.
Restart the daemon.

tests.measure: The set of IDs that answered.

gate.FAIL: any ID missing, any duplicate, or any unexpected ID
gate.CD: an ID answers intermittently — that is a wiring or bus-integrity fault, not a pass; take it to the scope

tests.gate_basis: Fifteen servo IDs from JOINT_IDS in model.rs:15-19; ID 200 is the imu_to_dxl v2 board, which robotd sync_reads FIRST every tick (bus.rs:92). The cheatsheet's own warning applies: `robotd init` needs the daemon stopped, because two writers on one UART corrupt each other's replies.

tests.title: Free travel and mechanical stops
tests.purpose: Confirm every joint can reach its commanded range before a policy asks it to.
pre: SV-03 PASS. Torque off on every servo. Robot on the stand.

steps.do: With torque off, move each joint slowly by hand from one end of its MJCF range to the other while logging Present Position(132).
Note where a hard stop is met, in counts and in degrees.

tests.measure: Per joint: minimum and maximum reachable position, in counts and degrees, and where a hard stop was met.

gate.PASS: every joint reaches both ends of its MJCF range (section 4.1) and meets no hard stop inside it
gate.FAIL: a hard stop inside the range, or a discontinuity in the sweep (a slipping horn or a dead encoder segment)

tests.gate_basis: Ranges are the MJCF joint limits read off Pollen's own robot_walk.xml via our simulation (out/sim/report.md, 'Joint range use'), in radians. Section 4.1 states each one in radians, degrees and encoder counts.

tests.title: Home-pose verification
tests.purpose: The single strongest calibration check on the whole robot: fifteen joints against fifteen published numbers.
pre: SV-04 PASS. Robot ON THE STAND - init moves every joint.

steps.do: Power the joints and ramp to the home pose (about 2 s).
steps.expect: the robot reaches the home pose

steps.do: Let it settle 3 s, then log 100 ticks.
Compare the mean Present Position of each joint against the expected counts in section 4.1.

tests.measure: Per joint: mean Present Position(132) over 100 ticks, in counts; the deviation from the expected home count.

gate.PASS: every joint within +/- 11 counts (+/- 1.0 deg) of its expected home count
gate.FAIL: any joint outside +/- 11 counts
gate.CD: a joint whose sign is inverted relative to the table - see the basis note; this is expected on the FIRST unit and must be resolved into a per-joint inversion table, not waved through

tests.gate_basis: Expected counts are computed here as 2048 + rad x 4096/(2 pi) from DEFAULT_POSITION in model.rs:39-55, which model.rs itself says 'must match HOME_FRAME in the training env - a policy is trained against these angles and observes joint positions relative to them, so a discrepancy here is a constant offset on 14 observation slots'. THE ONE ASSUMPTION: this mapping assumes servo-positive equals joint-positive with no inversion, and no published source gives a per-joint inversion table. On the first unit, a joint that lands the same distance the WRONG side of 2048 is an inversion, not a calibration error; record it, and this plan gains a measured inversion column.

tests.title: Mouth travel (ID 34)
tests.purpose: The mouth is in no policy, so nothing else exercises it.
pre: SV-05 PASS.

steps.do: Drive ID 34 to MOUTH_CLOSED and hold 2 s.
Drive ID 34 to MOUTH_OPEN and hold 2 s.
Read Present Current(126) at both ends.
Cycle 10 times.

tests.measure: Present Position(132) at both ends (counts and degrees); Present Current(126) at both ends (mA); drift over 10 cycles.

gate.PASS: both ends reached within +/- 11 counts, Present Current below 1750 mA at both ends, drift over 10 cycles <= 11 counts
gate.FAIL: either end not reached, or current at the limit (the jaw is binding)

tests.gate_basis: MOUTH_CLOSED = -5 deg and MOUTH_OPEN = +30 deg, verbatim constants in model.rs:63-64, reused from microduck_runtime's variant.rs. model.rs:31 names MOUTH_INDEX = 9 and states the omission is deliberate: every alpha policy is 14 actions with this joint skipped.

sections.lede: Fifteen servos and one IMU board share one wire. Two EEPROM values must be set per servo at build time, because neither can be assigned over a shared bus; everything else robotd asserts at every boot. Mechanical zero is set by assembly, not by a register - robotd never writes a homing offset.

sections.title: Sensor checks

tests.title: I2C3 roll-call
tests.purpose: Four addresses on one bus. Any absence names its own part.
pre: Board booted, overlays applied (setup-board.sh has run and the board has rebooted).

steps.do: Scan the HAT's I2C bus.

tests.measure: The set of 7-bit addresses that answer on /dev/i2c-3 (also reachable as /dev/i2c-pihat).

gate.PASS: 0x18, 0x19, 0x29 and 0x68 all answer
gate.FAIL: 0x18 absent (codec) or 0x29 absent (ToF)
gate.CD: 0x19/0x68 absent - the head IMU is a BMI088 on OUR reading of the overlay and it is described there as 'dormant', 'unused but still connected'. Whether a production head carries it is CANNOT DETERMINE (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md 4.2). Record the absence; do not fail the unit on it

tests.gate_basis: Addresses from Pollen's own device-tree overlays: codec 0x18 (compatible ti,tlv320aic3x), BMI088 0x19 and 0x68, ToF 0x29 via the HAT's Stemma J5. The bus is I2C3 M0 on header pins 3 and 5, GPIO1_A0 SDA / GPIO1_A1 SCL, 400 kHz, with one 10 k pull-up pair R12/R13. Note the ToF's other documented address, 0x52, is the same address written 8-bit.

tests.title: BMI088 identity
tests.purpose: Two fixed bytes that prove the part is the part.
pre: SN-01 shows 0x19 and 0x68.

steps.do: Read the accelerometer chip ID.
Read the gyroscope chip ID.

tests.measure: Two bytes.

gate.PASS: 0x1E at 0x19 register 0x00 and 0x0F at 0x68 register 0x00
gate.FAIL: either byte differs - a different part is fitted
gate.CD: the addresses did not answer in SN-01

tests.gate_basis: BMI088 datasheet BST-BMI088-DS000-19 Rev 1.9 (01/2024): 5.3.1 Register 0x00: ACC_CHIP_ID, reset value 0x1E, 'Contains identifier code of acceleration sensor' (page 26); 5.5.1 Register 0x00: GYRO_CHIP_ID, reset value 0x0F, 'Contains identifier code of gyroscope' (page 37). Caution from the same sheet: after an SPI-mode transition the first read is a dummy; on I2C this does not apply.

tests.title: BMI088 self-test, accelerometer and gyroscope
tests.purpose: Deflect the seismic mass and see it move; trigger the gyro's built-in test and read the verdict.
pre: SN-02 PASS. The robot STATIONARY and level - the accelerometer self-test superimposes on gravity, so the sheet requires static conditions.

steps.do: Set +/-24 g range: write 0x03 to ACC_RANGE (0x41).
Set ODR 1.6 kHz, continuous, normal (norm_avg4): write 0xA7 to ACC_CONF (0x40).
Wait > 2 ms.
Positive polarity: write 0x0D to ACC_SELF_TEST (0x6D). Wait > 50 ms. Read the three axes.
Negative polarity: write 0x09 to ACC_SELF_TEST (0x6D). Wait > 50 ms. Read the three axes.
Disable: write 0x00 to ACC_SELF_TEST (0x6D). Wait > 50 ms. Reset the device.
Gyro: set bit 0 (bite_trig) in GYRO_SELF_TEST (0x3C). Poll bit 1 (bist_rdy), then read bit 2 (bist_fail).
Read bit 4 of GYRO_SELF_TEST - the continuous background test.

tests.measure: Per axis: |positive response - negative response| in mg. Gyro: bist_rdy, bist_fail, background bit.

gate.PASS: x >= 1000 mg, y >= 1000 mg, z >= 500 mg, gyro bist_fail = 0 and the background bit = 1
gate.FAIL: any axis below its minimum, or bist_fail = 1
gate.CD: the part is absent - see SN-01

tests.gate_basis: Every step and every number is the vendor's own recommended procedure and Table 9, BST-BMI088-DS000-19 Rev 1.9, section 4.6.1 and 4.6.2, pages 17-18 of 62. The sheet also says: reset the device after a self-test, because the self-test response affects interrupt generation.

tests.title: Control IMU (imu_to_dxl, ID 200) - behavioural
tests.purpose: The IMU that actually flies the robot cannot be self-tested from the host. Test what it does instead.
pre: SV-03 PASS. robotd running. Robot on the stand, upright and still.

steps.do: Log 30 s of the state stream with the robot upright and still.
Read projected gravity in the trunk frame.
Lay the robot on its right side by hand, hold 5 s, log.
steps.expect: gravity moves onto the y axis

steps.do: Rotate 90 deg about the trunk yaw axis, hold 5 s, log.
steps.expect: gravity z unchanged, gyro shows the rotation

steps.do: Check the stale-read counter on the health row.

tests.measure: Projected gravity (unit vector) in each pose; gyro peak during each move (rad/s); the stale-read count over 30 s.

gate.PASS: upright gravity z <= -0.98 and |x|,|y| <= 0.10; gravity follows every imposed rotation; stale reads = 0 over 30 s
gate.FAIL: gravity does not follow a rotation, or the stale-read warning fires (25 identical 12-byte blocks in a row = 0.5 s)
gate.CD: an all-zero quaternion at start-up: the SFLP table has not been written yet. robotd keeps the last good value and never snaps to identity. Wait for 25 live blocks (about 0.25 s at 100 Hz) before judging

tests.gate_basis: The block at address 124 is: bytes 0..6 gyro x/y/z i16 LE at +/-500 dps, 17.5 mdps/LSB; bytes 6..12 the SFLP game-rotation quaternion x/y/z as IEEE fp16 with w reconstructed (imu.rs:8-17). Mount quaternion [0.7071, 0, 0.7071, 0] = +90 deg about Y; trunk = [+raw_z, +raw_y, -raw_x] (imu.rs:76-83). Fall detection may not trust the board until 25 live blocks have arrived (imu.rs:96-100), and the stale tracker warns after 25 identical blocks (bus.rs:49-58). The 0.98 / 0.10 numbers are decisions of this plan: no source states a static-accuracy figure for the assembled robot. NOTE the cheatsheet's own trap - 'a board that has stopped fusing keeps answering the bus, so nothing errors and the gravity vector holds a plausible attitude indefinitely'; the stale count is the only thing that catches it, which is why it is in the gate.

tests.title: LSM6DSV16X chip self-test - board incoming only
tests.purpose: Record what a register-level IMU self-test would be, and why it cannot run on an assembled robot.
pre: An imu_to_dxl board on a bench fixture with direct SPI or I2C to the LSM6DSV16X.
tool: a bench fixture with SPI/I2C to the IMU - see the gate

steps.do: Read WHO_AM_I (0Fh).
Enable accelerometer self-test: ST_XL_[1:0] in CTRL10 (19h) - 01 positive, 10 negative, 00 normal.
Enable gyroscope self-test: ST_G_[1:0] in the same register.
With the device stationary, take |OUTPUT(self-test enabled) - OUTPUT(self-test disabled)| per axis.

tests.measure: WHO_AM_I byte; accelerometer output change in mg; angular-rate output change in dps.

gate.PASS: WHO_AM_I = 0x70; accelerometer change within 50 - 1700 mg; angular-rate change within 20 - 80 dps at FS +/-250 dps, or 150 - 700 dps at FS +/-2000 dps
gate.FAIL: WHO_AM_I differs, or any change outside its window
gate.CD: THE EXPECTED VERDICT ON AN ASSEMBLED ROBOT. The LSM6DSV16X is not on any host bus: it sits behind an unidentified MCU on Pollen's imu_to_dxl v2 board, which presents it as a Dynamixel Protocol-2 slave at ID 200. No published register path reaches the chip, and no schematic, BOM or firmware for that board exists. On a built robot the IMU test is SN-04

tests.gate_basis: LSM6DSV16X datasheet DS13510 Rev 4: 9.13 WHO_AM_I (0Fh) 'value is fixed at 70h'; 9.23 CTRL10 (19h), Table 72/73, page 74 of 198, bits ST_G_[1:0] and ST_XL_[1:0] with 00 normal / 01 positive sign / 10 negative sign / 11 reserved. Vst from the electrical-characteristics table: linear acceleration self-test output change 50 to 1700 mg; angular rate self-test output change 20 to 80 dps at FS +/-250 dps and 150 to 700 dps at FS +/-2000 dps, defined with the device stationary as the absolute difference between self-test enabled and disabled.

tests.title: ToF ranging
tests.purpose: A real distance against a real target, at the vendor's own accuracy figure.
pre: SN-01 shows 0x29. tofd running. Head levelled, beak pointing at the target.
tool: Steel rule or laser distance meter

steps.do: Place the target normal to the beak at 500 mm, measured to the sensor's front face. Room lighting below 5 klx; note the level.
Open the ToF matrix.
steps.cmd: robotctl monitor  then press  t  for the ToF matrix
steps.expect: the 8x8 grid, header naming the sensor and 15 Hz

steps.do: Record the header line: it names the sensor generation, the rate, the zones ranged and the near-far span.
Record the mean of the centre four zones over 30 frames.
Repeat at 200 mm and at 1000 mm.
Point at open space and confirm the grid shows `.` (measured, nothing in range) and not `x` (could not measure).

tests.measure: Per distance: number of zones ranged out of 64; the mean and standard deviation of the centre four zones, in mm.

gate.PASS: at each distance, >= 56 of 64 zones ranged, and the centre-four mean within +/- 7 % of the reference distance
gate.FAIL: fewer than 56 zones, or the mean outside +/- 7 %
gate.CD: the header says `no sensor:` - tofd is up and nothing answered on the bus. Go back to SN-01

tests.gate_basis: +/- 7 % = the vendor's +/- 5 % (8x8 at 15 Hz, 201-4000 mm, white 88 % target, dark) plus the vendor's own stated 'additional 1~2 %' for PCB assembly tilt and mounting in a product housing. BOTH generations give the same +/- 5 % figure at this mode and range - VL53L8CX DS14161 Rev 12 Table 20 page 25, and VL53L5CX DS13754 Rev 13 Table 21 page 23 - so this gate holds even though which generation ships is CANNOT DETERMINE. Both are 45 deg x 45 deg detection volume, 65 deg diagonal. 56/64 is a decision of this plan; ST publishes no zone-yield figure, and Pollen's own example header shows 48/64 ranged in an ordinary room, so a full 64 must not be demanded. Read the last column of the theremin readout for the per-zone ST status codes if zones are missing: robotctl monitor's grid is STRICTER than the theremin - it marks anything outside status 5/9 as `x`, and a grid full of `x` does not mean the sensor is broken.

tests.title: Camera capture and hardware encode
tests.purpose: Sensor to a WebRTC-negotiable stream, with an exact byte count in the middle of it.
pre: Overlay radxa-zero3-rpi-camera-v2 applied and the board rebooted.
setup-gstreamer.sh has run.

steps.do: Confirm the sensor identified itself.
steps.expect: `imx219 2-0010: Model ID 0x0219, Lot ID ..., Chip ID 0x0773`

steps.do: Find the capture node by card name, not by number - node numbers are not stable across boots.
Capture 10 frames of 720p NV12 to a file.
Encode a test pattern in hardware and read the profile back.
steps.cmd: gst-launch-1.0 -v videotestsrc num-buffers=60 ! video/x-raw,format=NV12,width=1280,height=720,framerate=30/1 ! mpph264enc profile=baseline ! h264parse ! fakesink

steps.do: Confirm the encoder is reachable without root: /dev/mpp_service and /dev/rga at 660 root:video and the user in `video`.
steps.expect: gst-inspect-1.0 mpph264enc answers as that user

tests.measure: The dmesg identity line; the captured byte count; the profile h264parse negotiates.

gate.PASS: the identity line appears, the capture is exactly 13,824,000 bytes, and h264parse reports constrained-baseline
gate.FAIL: any of the three
gate.CD: no /dev/video* at all - that is ALSO exactly what an unattached camera looks like; check the ribbon before blaming the overlay

tests.gate_basis: 13,824,000 bytes = 10 frames x 1280 x 720 x 1.5 (NV12), and it is the exact figure Pollen measured on hardware for --stream-count=10 at 720p NV12. The identity string is Pollen's own probe output. The profile check is theirs too: profile=baseline turns CABAC and the 8x8 transform off, MPP emits no FMO/ASO/redundant slices, and the SPS carries profile_idc=66 with constraint_set1_flag, so h264parse's src pad negotiates constrained-baseline. Two traps from the same page: capture must NOT use v4l2src (the rkisp driver hands it a 2-buffer pool, it requeues too slowly and drops every third frame - about 20 fps from a 30 fps sensor); and nothing in the pipeline rotates, even though the IMX219 is mounted upside down, because videoflip cost 22 fps, 5522 RGA failures and 97 degC in one measured session.

tests.title: Audio loopback
tests.purpose: A tone out of the speaker and back in through the microphone, on the one card this robot has.
pre: SN-01 shows 0x18. The aic3104 overlay applied and the board rebooted.
A quiet room. The measurement microphone or a laptop 200 mm from the beak.

steps.do: Confirm the card exists.
Play a 1000 Hz sine for 3 s through the codec.
Record 3 s from the codec's own capture device while the tone plays.
FFT the recording. Find the peak bin and the median magnitude.
Ask the robot for its own voice.
steps.expect: a quack, in a voice seeded from this board's SoC serial

tests.measure: Peak frequency (Hz); peak-to-median magnitude ratio (dB); whether `robotctl quack` produced sound.

gate.PASS: peak within 1000 +/- 10 Hz, peak-to-median >= 20 dB, and `robotctl quack` sounds
gate.FAIL: no peak at 1 kHz, or `robotctl quack` reports no voice bank
gate.CD: the codec answers on I2C but ALSA has no card - the I2S3 side is the suspect, not the I2C side; MCLK is a fixed-clock node at 12 MHz and the cpu-dai sysclk is 12.288 MHz (256 x 48 kHz), and whether MCLK comes from a crystal on the HAT or an SoC pin is CANNOT DETERMINE

tests.gate_basis: The card name, the ALSA device (plughw:aic3104), the 12 MHz MCLK and the 12.288 MHz sysclk are all from Pollen's own aic3104-i2c3.dts and robotd.toml [audio]. The 1000 +/- 10 Hz and 20 dB figures are decisions of this plan: the fitted microphone and speaker have NO manufacturer part number in any source (both CANNOT DETERMINE in the component verification), the microphone is analog on the codec's Mic3R PGA input rather than a digital I2S part, and no amplifier is identified - so no acoustic figure can be cited and the gate is deliberately functional. `robotctl quack` is in the gate because a robot with no voice says so rather than printing a duck, which makes silence unambiguous.

tests.title: NFC - NO TEST EXISTS
tests.purpose: Record that this cannot be tested, and exactly what would change that.

steps.do: None. This row exists so the absence is on the record rather than missing from it.

tests.measure: Nothing.

gate.CD: CANNOT DETERMINE, and it is the answer, not a gap in this plan

tests.gate_basis: The press kit says 'two antennas, one in the head and one in the beak' and Pollen sells NFC tags and an NFC E-Ink 'Polaroid' tapped on the robot's head. But there is NO NFC code in the published runtime: a grep of duck-ipc-proto_lib.rs and of research/microduck-elec-grep.txt returns 0 hits for nfc, pn532 and st25. No reader IC is named, no bus, no antenna geometry. Two candidate readers were datasheeted on the shelf and neither is confirmed fitted: ST25R3916 (DS12484 Rev 8, two single-ended antenna drives - which would suit two antennas) and PN7150 (Rev 4.2, NCI over I2C, ONE antenna path). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a teardown identifying the reader IC and its bus, or a later release of pollen-robotics/microduck that exposes an NFC service. Until then there is nothing to command and nothing to read back.

tests.title: Camera-use indicator LED - NO TEST EXISTS
tests.purpose: Same, for the REC light.

steps.do: None.

tests.measure: Nothing.

gate.CD: CANNOT DETERMINE

tests.gate_basis: The press kit describes 'a dedicated camera-use indicator inspired by classic REC lights'. A source grep returns 0 hits: no GPIO, no driver, no LED class device is named anywhere in the published runtime. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a teardown tracing the LED to a header pin, or `ls /sys/class/leds` on a production board with the camera streaming.

sections.lede: Four devices on one I2C bus, a camera on MIPI CSI, an IMU that is only reachable through the servo bus, and two subsystems that cannot be tested at all. The last two rows are as much a part of this plan as the first eight.

sections.title: Control-loop and daemon acceptance

tests.title: Version agreement
tests.purpose: A daemon serving old code after an update looks exactly like a bug in the fix you just shipped.
pre: Board provisioned; updaterd, robotd, configd, btd, padd enabled.

steps.do: Print what every daemon is RUNNING against what is INSTALLED.
List the release store.
steps.expect: current points at the intended release

tests.measure: Per daemon: running version, installed version, git revision.

gate.PASS: every daemon runs the installed release and `robotctl version` prints no disagreement
gate.FAIL: any disagreement

tests.gate_basis: The cheatsheet's first instruction: 'Run this before believing any other diagnosis'. `version` shows the live release per component, never the store - the store is the `ls` above.

tests.title: Health verdict
tests.purpose: The one verdict the update system rolls back on.
pre: SV-03 PASS. Joints powered (robotctl robot init) - an unpowered bench board reporting unhealthy is the honest answer, not a failed build.

steps.do: Take the full report.
Read the loop section beside the verdict: achieved rate, missed deadlines, bus errors, IMU stale counters, battery, servo and board temperature.

tests.measure: Verdict; achieved loop rate (Hz); missed-deadline count; consecutive bus errors; IMU stale count; battery V and %; hottest servo and board temperature.

gate.PASS: healthy, with achieved rate >= 45.0 Hz and consecutive bus errors < 10
gate.FAIL: unhealthy, or degraded with a reason naming the bus or the loop
gate.CD: degraded on an unpowered bench board - that is what degraded exists to say; power the joints and re-run

tests.gate_basis: The thresholds are robotd's own [update_gate] defaults, with Pollen's stated reasons: min_achieved_hz = 45.0 ('90 % of the default 50 Hz: loose enough not to trip on one slow tick, tight enough that a loop dropping every tenth cycle is not called healthy'); max_consecutive_errors = 10 ('one dropped transaction is ordinary on a serial bus; a run of them means the bus is gone'). Battery and motor temperature appear on the report but MUST NOT reach the verdict - Pollen's own rule, because a release must never be rolled back for the state of the board it landed on.

tests.title: Loop rate over a window
tests.purpose: A loop running at 60 % of target is alive, answers every request, and is badly broken.
pre: SW-02 PASS. Joints powered, robot on the stand, policy enabled.

steps.do: Log 300 s at 50 Hz. Redirected, monitor prints one line per tick.
Compute the achieved-rate distribution and the largest gap between ticks.

tests.measure: Achieved rate: mean, 5th percentile, minimum (Hz). Largest inter-tick gap (ms). Missed-deadline count.

gate.PASS: 5th-percentile achieved rate >= 45.0 Hz AND no inter-tick gap >= 500 ms
gate.FAIL: either

tests.gate_basis: 45.0 Hz is min_achieved_hz. 500 ms is stall_periods = 25 at 50 Hz - 'a loop silent that long is genuinely gone'. Pollen note the original stall_periods of 3 (60 ms) tripped on ordinary scheduler jitter, and 'a health check that trips on jitter rolls back good releases'. The 5th percentile is a decision of this plan: robotd's own gate is on the achieved rate it computes, and a percentile over a 300 s window is the closest fixed-window equivalent.

tests.title: Policy load
tests.purpose: A policy that will not load is unhealthy, and the reason is printed.
pre: SW-02 PASS.

steps.do: Read the bottom border of the monitor - it names the .onnx files loaded and whether a standing network is configured at all.
Confirm the observation shape is the 61-D alpha contract, not the 51-D legacy net (which is refused at load).

tests.measure: The policy file names on the border; the health verdict.

gate.PASS: the border names the configured policies and health is healthy
gate.FAIL: the border reports a policy that would not load, and health is unhealthy with the searched path named
gate.CD: policy.enabled = false - a legitimate configuration, healthy, holding whatever pose the robot started in. Not a degraded state. Set it true before WK

tests.gate_basis: Nine ONNX policies are published on huggingface.co/pollen-robotics/microduck-policies. The alpha observation is obs[1,61] -> actions[1,14]: gyro(3) | projected_gravity(3) | joint_pos(14) | joint_vel(14) | last_action(14) | command(13), with joint positions RELATIVE to DEFAULT_POSITION - which is why SV-05 matters to this test. policy.enabled separates 'no policy wanted' (healthy) from 'policy broken' (unhealthy).

tests.title: Deadman
tests.purpose: Losing the client must leave a biped standing, not walking.
pre: SW-04 PASS. Pad paired and driving. Robot on the floor, walking.

steps.do: Drive forward, then kill padd while the stick is held forward.
steps.expect: the robot stops walking and stands

steps.do: Read the monitor: the reason is spelled out, not named.
steps.expect: `deadman - no intent arrived recently, velocity zeroed`

steps.do: Measure the time from the last pad packet to zero commanded velocity, from the log.
Restart padd.

tests.measure: Time from last intent to zero commanded velocity, ms.

gate.PASS: velocity zeroed within 500 ms and the robot is left STANDING, not limp
gate.FAIL: the robot keeps walking, or goes limp

tests.gate_basis: deadman_ms = 500, and Pollen's own words on why it stops rather than limps: 'losing contact with a client should leave a biped standing, because standing is its safe state'. There is no stop button by design - release the sticks and it stands.

sections.lede: Pollen built the control loop before anything that walks, so that health would be a real measurement rather than a ping. These four tests read that measurement back.

sections.title: Walk acceptance

tests.title: Stand and hold
tests.purpose: Before it walks, it must stand still.
pre: SW-04 PASS. Robot on the FLOOR (off the stand) on the surface defined in section 7.1. Pack charged above 7.5 V.

steps.do: Power the joints and ramp to the home pose.
Log 30 s with no command.
Mark the start and end position of the mid-foot; measure the drift.

tests.measure: Maximum trunk tilt over 30 s (deg); drift of the mid-foot (mm); falls.

gate.PASS: no fall, maximum tilt <= 10.0 deg, drift <= 50 mm over 30 s
gate.FAIL: a fall, or tilt beyond 10.0 deg

tests.gate_basis: SIMULATION REFERENCE, measured on our own MuJoCo run stand_hold_ours (out/sim/report.md): 4 s holding STAND, walked 0.003 m, maximum tilt 1.4 deg, trunk z 0.115 -> 0.116 m, no fall, 0 self-contacts. The 10.0 deg and 50 mm gates are DECISIONS of this plan, set far outside the simulated figures to leave room for sim-to-real transfer and for the real floor; they are not measurements of any robot. The first built unit's measured tilt and drift replace them.

tests.title: Walk acceptance
tests.purpose: The headline test: does a built unit walk.
pre: WK-01 PASS. Pad paired. Surface per section 7.1, levelled and measured.
A 1200 mm run marked on the surface with a start line.
tool: steel rule or laser distance meter

steps.do: Place the robot with the mid-foot on the start line, facing along the run.
Enable the policy (Start) and hold the left stick fully forward for 8.0 s. The commanded forward velocity is 0.25 m/s - the value the browser simulator uses as VEL_FWD.
Log the whole run.
Measure the straight-line distance from the start line to the mid-foot at the moment the stick is released.
Read the maximum trunk tilt and the fall flag from the log.

tests.measure: Walked distance in 8.0 s (m, 3 dp); mean speed (m/s); maximum trunk tilt (deg); falls; maximum |joint velocity| (rad/s); pack current mean and peak (A).

gate.PASS: walked >= 0.594 m in 8.0 s AND no fall AND maximum tilt <= 25.842 deg
gate.FAIL: any of the three
gate.CD: the robot walks but the distance cannot be measured to 1 mm because the path curved off the run - re-run with a longer surface; a curved path is a real result and belongs in the log

tests.gate_basis: SIMULATION REFERENCE, measured on our own run walk_ours (out/sim/report.md, MuJoCo 3.12.0, Pollen's alpha_walking.onnx, 50 Hz, timestep 0.005 s, decimation 4): 0.7925 m in 8 s, mean 0.1053 m/s, maximum tilt 4.11 deg, no fall, 0 self-contacts, contacts mean 1.92, maximum joint speed 5.74 rad/s at the left knee, 0 frames within 1 deg of any limit. The stock and swapped-mesh models produced BIT-IDENTICAL trajectories, so the reference is Pollen's physics and not ours. THE 0.594 m GATE IS A DECISION OF THIS PLAN: 75 % of the simulated 0.7925 m, an allowance for sim-to-real transfer that NO source measures - no real-robot walk distance exists anywhere in this repository or in Pollen's published material. The 25.842 deg tilt gate IS derived: limp_fall_tilt_z = -0.90 in robotd.toml, and acos(0.90) = 25.842 deg, the tilt at which the daemon itself decides a fall has started. DO NOT TEST AT 0.15 m/s: our own velocity sweep on Pollen's stock model measured vx 0.05 -> 0.003 m, 0.10 -> 0.007 m, 0.15 -> 0.008 m, 0.20 -> 0.011 m, 0.25 -> 0.792 m, 0.30 -> 0.940 m, 0.40 -> 1.281 m in 8 s. Everything below 0.25 sits inside the walking policy's stand-still band and a robot that correctly stands still would read as a failure.

tests.title: Walk repeatability
tests.purpose: One walk is an anecdote.
pre: WK-02 PASS once.

steps.do: Repeat WK-02 five times, returning the robot to the start line between runs. Do not recharge between runs; record the pack voltage before each.

tests.measure: Five distances (m, 3 dp); five maximum tilts (deg); falls out of five; pack voltage before each run (V).

gate.PASS: 5 of 5 runs meet the WK-02 gate, and the spread of the five distances is <= 0.150 m
gate.FAIL: any fall, or any run below 0.594 m

tests.gate_basis: The 0.150 m spread is a decision of this plan; no source publishes run-to-run variance for this robot, and our simulation is deterministic (the stock and swapped models were bit-identical), so it can offer none. Pack voltage is recorded per run because voltage_adapt is OFF by default, so the servos' effective stiffness tracks the pack as it sags and a five-run sequence walks progressively softer.

tests.title: Get up
tests.purpose: Knock it over and it stands itself up.
pre: WK-02 PASS.

steps.do: Sit, then stand, with DPad-Down. Three cycles.
Lay the robot face down on the surface, release, and let the standing policy recover it. Three attempts.
Repeat face up. Three attempts.
Log all nine.

tests.measure: Per attempt: time from release to standing (s); final trunk height (m); final tilt (deg); success.

gate.PASS: 9 of 9 recover, each within 6.0 s, ending at trunk height >= 0.100 m and tilt <= 10.0 deg
gate.FAIL: any attempt that does not recover within 6.0 s

tests.gate_basis: SIMULATION REFERENCE (out/sim/report.md): stand_from_sit_ours over 6 s ended at trunk z 0.116 m with maximum tilt 5.0 deg and no fall; stand_from_fold_ours over 6 s ended at trunk z 0.116 m. The 6.0 s window is the simulated run length; the 0.100 m and 10.0 deg gates are decisions of this plan, set below and above the simulated 0.116 m and 5.0 deg. Pollen's own note applies: the standing policy 'is a good stand-up-er and a bad faller' - from a STILL robot, face down or face up, it gets back on its feet cleanly, which is exactly the condition this test creates and exactly what limp_fall exists to create after a real fall.

tests.title: Limp-fall behaviour
tests.purpose: Prove the fleet lands soft.
pre: WK-04 PASS. [safety] limp_fall = true (the default since it was validated on a robot).
A soft landing area - this test deliberately drops the robot.

steps.do: Walk, then tip the robot past the trigger tilt by hand and let go.
steps.expect: the gains drop before it lands

steps.do: Watch the state stream for safety.limp and the limp_fall / limp_pose policy labels.
Let it come to rest, then watch the pose ramp and the hand-back to the standing policy.

tests.measure: Whether limp_fall armed before ground contact; time from arming to still; time of the pose ramp; whether the robot stood afterwards.

gate.PASS: limp_fall arms before ground contact, the robot arrives limp, ramps to the standing pose and stands, in 3 of 3 attempts
gate.FAIL: the robot lands stiff (the policy fought the floor), or does not stand afterwards
gate.CD: limp_fall = false on this board - then this test does not apply and the robot's behaviour is the prototype's: the policy keeps driving and the humans stay in charge

tests.gate_basis: Every threshold is robotd.toml [safety]: trigger when already tilted past limp_fall_tilt_z = -0.90 (25.842 deg), still tipping rather than recovering, and a limp_fall_lookahead_ms = 300 extrapolation of projected gravity lands past limp_fall_predict_z = -0.5 (60.000 deg); debounce limp_fall_debounce_ms = 60, three ticks at 50 Hz. Then gain_limp = 50 until still (limp_fall_still_rate = 1.0 rad/s for limp_fall_still_ms = 200) or limp_fall_max_ms = 1500 whichever comes first, then a limp_fall_pose_ms = 600 ramp at limp_fall_pose_gain = 160. Separately, the fall REPORT (not the gate) is fall_gravity_z = -0.5 debounced 200 ms.

tests.title: Post-walk thermal
tests.purpose: The one number every servo publishes about its own health.
pre: WK-03 complete - five 8 s walks back to back.

steps.do: Immediately after the fifth walk, read Present Temperature(146) for all fifteen servos and the board temperature.
Repeat after 5 minutes of standing.

tests.measure: Fifteen servo temperatures (degC, 1 degC resolution) and the board temperature, at both times.

gate.PASS: every servo below 70 degC and no Overheating latch
gate.FAIL: any servo at or above 70 degC, or any servo latched

tests.gate_basis: 70 degC is Temperature Limit(31)'s initial value and the top of the vendor's operating range (-5 to +70 degC, E1 Specifications). Shutdown(63) = 52 as robotd writes it keeps Bit 2 Overheating Error set, so the servo LATCHES at that point rather than degrading quietly. Separately, the SoC has a measured thermal wall of its own: Pollen recorded 95-97 degC and a throttle to 408 MHz when the camera pipeline did the rotation in software, and the NPU duck detector runs at 2 Hz for the same reason - 'a thermal limit, not a preference'. Board temperature is a DESCRIPTION on the health report and may not reach any verdict.

sections.lede: The thresholds here come from our own MuJoCo runs of Pollen's published policies on Pollen's own physics. Where a gate is a simulation figure it says so; where a gate is an allowance for sim-to-real transfer it says that too, and names the fraction, because no real-robot walk figure exists in any source.

surface.title: 7.1 The surface
rows: the acceptance run is 0.594 m minimum with a start line and room to stop
within 1.0 deg, measured with a digital inclinometer, recorded in the log
the gate is a distance in a fixed time; a slope moves it and would not be visible in the data
hard, flat, dry, matte - laminate or sealed MDF. NOT carpet, NOT glass, NOT a rubber mat

the simulation's floor is rigid with foot friction 1.0 and condim 3 on the foot collision geoms only (constants.py). The friction coefficient of the real sole against any real surface is measured nowhere in this repository - CANNOT DETERMINE. A hard matte surface is the closest match that can be specified without measuring one
every servo figure and the pack's behaviour move with it, and none of the vendor current figures carries a temperature

eol: no short on any rail before power
every rail with a band inside it
SERVO_V measured at four points, both supply settings
no servo reaches Current Limit(38) = 1750 mA
every servo's eleven registers read back correct
fifteen joints within +/- 11 counts of home
BMI088 self-test x,y >= 1000 mg, z >= 500 mg, gyro bist_fail = 0
upright gravity z <= -0.98, stale reads 0 over 30 s
1000 +/- 10 Hz peak, >= 20 dB over median; robotctl quack sounds
every daemon runs the installed release
p05 rate >= 45.0 Hz over 300 s; no gap >= 500 ms
velocity zeroed within 500 ms, robot left standing
no fall in 30 s; tilt <= 10.0 deg; drift <= 50 mm
walked >= 0.594 m in 8.0 s; no fall; tilt <= 25.842 deg
every servo below 70 degC after five walks
logs: one directory per built unit, named by the serial the robot derives its own name from (`duck-` plus four characters from the SoC serial, `robotctl system info`)

every `robotctl monitor --json` capture. Redirected or piped, monitor prints one line per tick and the joint angles stay in RADIANS whatever the screen is set to - the on-screen degrees are a display choice, the file is not
`robotctl health --json` is the support bundle: hardware and software in one report
`robotctl update log` and /var/lib/robot/updater/runs/*.jsonl are fsync'ed per entry and OUTLIVE a power cut, which the journal on this board does not - /var/log is zram
`journalctl -u robotd -u mediad -u tofd -u padd -b` for the boot under test. Volatile: copy it into the unit's directory before the next boot
every meter reading, to 3 dp, with the probe points named. The rail survey and EB-04 in particular are the evidence that closes an open question in docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md 12

open.q: Are the XL330 servos fed the raw 2S pack, above their 6.0 V rating?
open.status: the test exists; no unit has been measured
open.settles: a meter on pin 2 of the servo bus with the pack fitted. Both outcomes are informative and one of them requires docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md 3.4 to be corrected.

open.q: What does a Microduck draw, walking?
open.status: no vendor figure exists between standby 17 mA and stall 1.47 A per servo, and no measured figure exists for the assembled robot
open.settles: EB-07 states A/B/C. Until then every rail budget in this repository rests on an assumption, including the 1 A-per-moving-servo basis behind the harness voltage-drop model in wiring/CABLES.md.

open.q: Which ToF generation ships, VL53L5CX or VL53L8CX?
open.status: CANNOT DETERMINE, and it does not block this plan
open.settles: the header line of `robotctl monitor`'s ToF block names the sensor - tofd picks the driver from an ID read. The +/- 5 % accuracy gate is identical for both parts at 8x8 / 15 Hz / 201-4000 mm, so the test passes or fails the same way either way.

open.q: Is the head IMU the HAT's BMI088, and does any shipped code read it?
open.status: CANNOT DETERMINE. The overlay calls it dormant, 'unused but still connected'
open.settles: i2cdetect finding 0x19 and 0x68 on a production board, plus a grep of the release binaries for any BMI088 access. SN-01 does the first half; the second half needs a shipped release.

open.q: What is the fitted microphone, speaker and amplifier?
open.status: CANNOT DETERMINE for all three. The component verification returned no manufacturer part number for either transducer
open.settles: a teardown. Until then the audio gate is functional, not acoustic, and no sensitivity, impedance or SPL figure may be asserted.

open.q: What is the NFC reader IC, and where are the two antennas?
open.status: CANNOT DETERMINE. Zero NFC hits in the published runtime
open.settles: a teardown, or a later release of pollen-robotics/microduck exposing an NFC service. Two candidates are datasheeted on our shelf and neither is confirmed: ST25R3916 (two single-ended antenna drives) and PN7150 (one antenna path).

open.q: Which GPIO drives the camera-use indicator LED?
open.status: CANNOT DETERMINE. Zero hits in a source grep
open.settles: `ls /sys/class/leds` on a production board with the camera streaming, or a teardown.

open.q: Does the robot charge in situ over USB-C with the pack fitted, and on which port?
open.settles: EB-08 on a unit. Note the shelf's reference 2S charger, MCP73213, needs roughly 8.7 V or more at its input, which 5 V USB cannot supply without a boost stage nobody has seen.

open.q: Is any joint's servo-positive direction inverted relative to the MJCF joint sign?
open.status: CANNOT DETERMINE. No published source gives a per-joint inversion table
open.settles: SV-05 on the first unit. A joint that lands the same distance the wrong side of 2048 is an inversion. The measured table becomes a column of section 4.1 and this plan is regenerated.

open.q: What does a real Microduck actually walk in 8 s at vx 0.25?
open.status: CANNOT DETERMINE. The 0.594 m gate is 75 % of our simulated 0.7925 m and the 75 % is a decision, not a measurement
open.settles: WK-02 and WK-03 on the first five built units. Replace the fraction with the measured mean minus three standard deviations and regenerate this document.

open.q: What is the friction coefficient of the sole against the acceptance surface?
open.status: CANNOT DETERMINE. The simulation uses foot friction 1.0, condim 3, on a rigid floor
open.settles: a coefficient-of-friction measurement of the printed TPU sole against the chosen bench material. Until then the surface is specified by description (hard, flat, matte) rather than by a number.

open.q: Can a chip-level IMU self-test be run at all on a built robot?
open.status: No. The LSM6DSV16X sits behind an unidentified MCU on an unpublished board
open.settles: Pollen publishing the imu_to_dxl v2 schematic and firmware, or a debug path on the board that exposes the chip. Until then SN-05 is an incoming test for the BOARD, and SN-04 is the only IMU test a finished robot can take.
